content_metadata.description: This video explores the unique structure, bonding, preparation, and reactions of Diborane (B2H6).

qAndA.answer: Diborane contains two types of bonds: B-H bonds (2-center-2-electron bond) and B-H-B bonds (3-center-2-electron bond also known as 'Banana bond').
qAndA.question: What type of bond is present in Diborane?

qAndA.answer: Diborane can be prepared by passing Boron trifluoride (BF3) through Lithium Aluminium hydride (LiAlH4).
qAndA.question: How is Diborane prepared in the laboratory?

qAndA.answer: The Boron atoms in Diborane undergo sp3 hybridization.
qAndA.question: What is the hybridization of Boron atoms in Diborane?

qAndA.answer: Diborane reacts with ammonia to form B3N3H6, also known as Borazole or 'Inorganic Benzene.'
qAndA.question: What is the product formed when Diborane reacts with ammonia on heating?

qAndA.answer: Borazole is called 'Inorganic Benzene' due to its similar structure and aromatic nature to Benzene, despite containing Boron and Nitrogen instead of Carbon.
qAndA.question: Why is Borazole referred to as 'Inorganic Benzene'?
